name: La Posa LTVA
stayLimit: Permit, not free. Fee season Sep 15–Apr 15: $180 season, $80 for 4 weeks, $40 for 2 weeks on the BLM pages. North, South, West, and Tyson Wash are the four La Posa units, about 2 miles south of Quartzsite on US-95.
hazards: soft shoulders off the graded roads
notes: The pin is the Quartzsite complex, not a reserved site. Self-contained rules apply. This is the seasonal public-land permit, not $0.

name: Imperial Dam LTVA
stayLimit: Permit, not free. Same BLM fee season: $180 / $80 / $40. Senator Wash Road off S-24, north of Yuma, California side of the river.
notes: Do not camp overnight in desert washes here. Pin is the LTVA approach, not a numbered site.

name: Pilot Knob LTVA
stayLimit: Permit, not free. Fee season Sep 15–Apr 15: $180 season, $80 for 4 weeks, $40 for 2 weeks. BLM also posts 14-day camping Apr 16–Sep 14. Self-contained only.
notes: I-8 to Sidewinder Road (exit 164), then south. Fort Yuma Indian Reservation borders nearby public land — reservation land is not a campsite.

name: Hot Springs LTVA
stayLimit: Permit required Sep 15–Apr 15 ($180 / $80 / $40). Not free. Self-contained only. BLM posts 14-day camping in the off-season window.
hazards: hot spring is not a swimming pool you can assume is open
notes: BLM directions: I-8 exit 131, east on Evan Hewes about 3.8 miles. The pin follows those directions. Confirm the entrance sign.

name: Tamarisk LTVA
stayLimit: Permit, not free. Fee season $180 / $80 / $40. Smallest of the El Centro LTVAs. Self-contained. Off-season 14-day rule is still not a home.
notes: GPS from Recreation.gov for this BLM site. I-8 to Highway 98 (exit 143), west about 2.7 miles, south on the dirt road.

name: Midland LTVA
stayLimit: Permit, not free. Same fee season. Self-contained only. BLM: do not camp within 2 miles outside the Midland boundary.
notes: From Blythe, Lovekin Road off I-10, then about 8 miles north. Midland-Rice Road. Pin is that approach.

name: Mule Mountain LTVA
stayLimit: Permit, not free. You may camp only at designated sites in Wiley's Well and Coon Hollow. One camping unit per site.
notes: BLM page for Wiley's Well, one of the two designated Mule Mountain LTVA campgrounds. Coon Hollow is the other: https://www.blm.gov/visit/coon-hollow-campground. Permit, designated sites only. This pin is not the Midland LTVA.

name: Angeles National Forest roads
stayLimit: Developed campgrounds (Chilao and others) charge a fee. Dispersed camping is only on roads the MVUM marks open, and fire closures wipe out a lot of seasons. Not a Santa Monica commute base.
notes: Honest closest public land to Los Angeles, and still a poor trailer-and-Tesla plan. The pin is the Chilao area. Read the current MVUM and closure map. Posted signs win.

name: Los Padres — Pine Mountain corridor
stayLimit: Dispersed only where the Los Padres MVUM says the road is open. Valley floors and ranch roads are often private. 14-day forest rules where camping is allowed.
notes: Not a free pad next to Ventura. The pin is a forest corridor, not a site. If a gate or sign says closed, it is closed.

name: Holcomb Valley, San Bernardino NF
stayLimit: Big Pine Flat and other developed sites are fee campgrounds. Dispersed spots follow the MVUM. Snow closes this in winter.
notes: High country north of Big Bear. January is the wrong month. Not a daily Santa Monica drive.

name: Joshua Tree National Park
stayLimit: Developed campgrounds and any backcountry board the park actually issues. This is not free roadside dispersed camping.
notes: Included so the park is not mistaken for BLM. The pin is the Oasis visitor center in Twentynine Palms, not a vacant site.

name: Death Valley National Park
stayLimit: Furnace Creek and the other named campgrounds are the overnight product. Backcountry camping needs the park's permit rules. Not free dispersed along the highway.
notes: Pin is Furnace Creek. Summer is a safety problem, not a bargain.

name: Lake Mead National Recreation Area
stayLimit: NPS recreation area. Camp in designated campgrounds. Shoreline dispersed camping is not the default.
notes: Pin is the Boulder Beach area. Do not treat the recreation-area boundary as boondocking.

name: Anza-Borrego — Blair Valley
stayLimit: Primitive camping inside Anza-Borrego follows state-park rules, not BLM 14-day custom. Some zones are closed to vehicles.
hazards: soft sand off the main track
notes: State park, not BLM. The pin is Blair Valley. Stay on the roads the park allows. Side tracks get sandy.

name: Owl Canyon Campground
stayLimit: Developed BLM campground at Rainbow Basin, with a fee. Not free dispersed in the fossil beds.
notes: Closest honest BLM campground toward LA is still Barstow, hours from Santa Monica. Confirm the fee on the BLM page.

name: Johnson Valley OHV
stayLimit: OHV area. 14 days in 28 where camping is open. Means of the Means dry lake and many tracks are soft.
notes: Hidden in Trailer + Tesla mode. A paved highway nearby is not the same as the OHV network.

name: El Mirage Dry Lake
stayLimit: Open OHV dry lake. The playa is soft. A permit or fee schedule may apply — read the current BLM page. Not a trailer pad.
notes: Hidden in Trailer + Tesla mode. Included so the dry lake is not mistaken for free parking.

name: Afton Canyon
stayLimit: BLM campground in the canyon plus nearby dispersed rules. Flash floods use this wash. Fee at the developed campground.
notes: Stay out of the live wash. The Mojave Road through here is a 4x4 route and is listed separately.

name: Mojave Road
stayLimit: Historic 4x4 road. 14-day dispersed rules only where you are actually on open public land and not in a closure.
notes: Hidden in Trailer + Tesla mode. Do not tow a travel trailer onto this road.

name: Corn Springs
stayLimit: Small BLM campground in the Chuckwalla Bench. Fee. Palm oasis. Not a long-term home.
notes: Confirm the current fee and whether the road matches your trailer. Pin is the campground.

name: Alabama Hills
stayLimit: Dispersed camping on designated or posted-open roads. 14-day limit. Movie Road itself is not a campground. Some spurs are sandy.
notes: Stay on graded roads if you are towing. If a spur looks soft, it is soft. Not a monthly.

name: Trona Pinnacles
stayLimit: Dispersed near the pinnacles, 14 days, no hookups. The dirt road is washboard and can rut.
notes: Tow only if you are willing to drive a rough graded road slowly. There is no dump at the pinnacles.

name: Fossil Falls
stayLimit: Developed BLM campground on Cinder Road. Fee. Lava and a short walk. Not dispersed across the flow.
notes: Cinder Road leaves US-395 south of the Coso Junction. Confirm the fee.

name: Panamint Valley
stayLimit: Dispersed on open BLM in the valley, 14 days. Wingate Road and Ballarat Road are the graded approaches. Side canyons get worse fast. Death Valley boundary is not BLM.
notes: Pin is the valley floor near Ballarat. Do not follow a two-track into the Panamints with a trailer.

name: Box Canyon / Mecca Hills
stayLimit: Dispersed where the route is open. The canyon road is a flood path. Ladder Canyon is a hike, not a camp.
notes: High clearance. A travel trailer does not belong in the narrows. Wilderness off the road is closed to vehicles.

name: Plomosa Road dispersed
stayLimit: 14 days in 28 on open BLM outside the La Posa LTVA boundary. Do not use this to dodge the LTVA permit buffer.
notes: North of Quartzsite. The pin is the road corridor. Check you are not inside an LTVA distance restriction.

name: Craggy Wash
stayLimit: Dispersed BLM north of Kingman. 14 days. Graded desert roads, no hookups.
notes: A known Kingman dispersed area. Still confirm the road and any fire restriction. Not a reserved site.

name: Burro Creek Campground
stayLimit: Developed BLM campground on US-93 between Kingman and Wikieup. Fee. Not dispersed in the campground loops.
notes: Paved approach off the highway. Confirm the fee and site length.

name: Dumont Dunes
stayLimit: OHV dunes. Permit or fee often required. Soft sand. Not a Tesla-and-trailer destination.
notes: Hidden in Trailer + Tesla mode.

name: Jawbone Canyon OHV
stayLimit: OHV area off Highway 14. Sandy canyon bottom. 14-day rules where camping is open.
notes: Closer to LA than Quartzsite and still the wrong surface for a travel trailer.

name: Imperial Sand Dunes
stayLimit: OHV dunes with a permit in season. Glamis and Gordon's Well are sand. Not an LTVA and not a trailer base.
notes: Hidden in Trailer + Tesla mode. A highway pullout is not the dunes.

name: Stoddard Valley OHV
stayLimit: OHV area south of Barstow. Rocky and sandy. 14 days where open.
notes: Hidden in Trailer + Tesla mode.

name: Rasor OHV
stayLimit: Open OHV area off I-15. Sand and power lines. Not a quiet camp.
notes: Hidden in Trailer + Tesla mode.

name: Red Rock Canyon NCA
stayLimit: Scenic drive has a fee. Camping is at the designated campground, not on the scenic loop.
notes: BLM, and still not 'camp wherever it is yellow.' Use the campground if you stay.

name: Gold Butte National Monument
stayLimit: Monument rules. Many roads are high clearance. 14-day dispersed only where roads are open. Whitney Pocket is the usual graded start.
notes: Do not tow past the graded entrance. The pin is the monument, not a site reservation.

name: Valley of Fire State Park
stayLimit: State park campground with an entrance fee. Not BLM dispersed.
notes: Included so the red rock is not filed under free public land.

name: Klondike Bluffs
stayLimit: BLM camping along the Klondike Bluffs road follows Moab field-office rules and stay limits. Not Arches National Park.
notes: Read the current Moab camping map. Zones change. The pin is the bluffs road, not a reserved site.

name: Dalton Wells
stayLimit: BLM area north of Moab. Stay limits and designated camping may apply. Check the field office map for the year you go.
notes: Graded approach. Still not a hookup park, and the rules tighten when Moab is crowded.

name: Horsethief Campground
stayLimit: Developed BLM campground on UT-313 toward Canyonlands Island in the Sky. Fee. Designated sites.
notes: Fee campground, not free dispersed on the mesa.

name: Sand Flats Recreation Area
stayLimit: Permit fee to enter. Slickrock and campsites are designated. Not free.
notes: Do not list this as $0. The permit is the product.

name: Gemini Bridges
stayLimit: High-clearance road and trails west of Moab. Parts are 4x4. Camp only where the field office allows.
notes: Shown as high clearance. Do not take the trailer down the trail itself.

name: Warner Valley
stayLimit: Dispersed BLM south of St. George and the Arizona line. 14 days. Graded roads. Fort Pearce is nearby and has its own rules.
notes: Pin is the valley. Stay off soft side tracks if you are towing.

name: 18 Road / North Fruita Desert
stayLimit: BLM camping zones north of Fruita. Stay limits and designated sites apply. Mountain-bike traffic. Not a monthly.
notes: Use the posted camping nodes. The pin is the 18 Road corridor.

name: Rabbit Valley
stayLimit: BLM recreation area on the Colorado–Utah line. Camp in signed areas. 14-day style limits. Dinosaur tracks are not a campsite.
notes: Graded. Rain turns the clay into a tow-out.

name: Bangs Canyon
stayLimit: South of Grand Junction. Rough roads. Camp only on open routes.
notes: High clearance. Leave the trailer in town.

name: Christmas Valley / Fort Rock country
stayLimit: Dispersed on open BLM around the Christmas Valley dune and lava country. Fort Rock State Natural Area is a separate fee site. 14 days.
notes: Stay off the dune face. The pin is the basin, not the state park.

name: Alvord Desert
stayLimit: Playa east of Steens Mountain. The surface is a dry lake. 14 days. Hot springs nearby are private or permitted — do not assume a soak.
notes: Hidden in Trailer + Tesla mode. A wet playa will bury a tow vehicle.

name: Steens Mountain loop
stayLimit: South loop is a high seasonal road. Developed BLM campgrounds charge. The loop is not a winter road and not a trailer tour.
notes: January drops this. July is the season, and it is still a mountain road.

name: Cascade Lakes Highway
stayLimit: Deschutes National Forest. Developed campgrounds are fees. Dispersed camping only on MVUM-open roads. Highway closes in winter.
notes: Pin is the high lakes corridor. Do not invent a free site between fee campgrounds. January: closed.

name: Bishop Creek, Inyo NF
stayLimit: Developed Inyo National Forest campgrounds charge a fee. Dispersed camping follows the MVUM and is limited. Snow into early summer.
notes: January drops the high Sierra. The pin is the creek canyon, not a vacant pad.

name: Ancient Bristlecone approach
stayLimit: Schulman Grove is a developed scenic site and the road closes in winter. Nearby White Mountains camping is forest rules, high, and cold.
notes: January: do not plan this. The pin is Schulman Grove.

name: Western Divide, Sequoia NF
stayLimit: Sequoia National Forest highway campgrounds are fees. Dispersed camping is MVUM-only. The Western Divide closes seasonally.
notes: High Sierra. January drops it. Nearest listed hub is Bishop and it is not close — resupply in the San Joaquin Valley before you climb.

name: Lac du Bois grasslands
stayLimit: Provincial Crown land near Kamloops. Often 14 consecutive days. Not a national Crown-land layer. Grassland roads and cattle range.
notes: The pin is the grassland north of Kamloops, not a reserved site. Use the B.C. recreation map. Posted range and private gates win.

name: Wells Gray corridor
stayLimit: Wells Gray Provincial Park campgrounds charge fees. Forest roads outside the park are a separate Crown-land rule, often 14 days, and many are high clearance.
notes: Do not treat the park boundary as free camping. Clearwater is the town. The pin is the park corridor.

name: St. Mary River country
stayLimit: East Kootenay. Provincial parks charge. Crown land outside them is typically 14 days and must be vacant public land, not a lakeshore lease.
notes: Region pin near Cranbrook. Open the B.C. iMap before you stay. This is not a campsite reservation.

name: Alberta Eastern Slopes public land
stayLimit: Public-land camping is typically 14 days where it is allowed. Public Land Use Zones, including Ghost country, have extra rules. Random camping is not legal on every acre.
notes: No hub in this file is close — Calgary is the town, and it is not listed as a resupply pin. Read the current PLUZ map. January drops the Rockies.

name: Thunder Bay Crown-land region
stayLimit: Up to 21 days where Crown land camping is open. Non-residents need a Crown land camping permit. Sleeping Giant is a provincial park and charges a fee.
notes: This pin is the region north of the city, not a legal site. Use the Crown Land Use Policy Atlas. Low confidence on purpose.

name: Yukon territorial land near Whitehorse
stayLimit: Camping on territorial land is allowed outside municipalities and posted closures. Highway campgrounds are a paid system. First Nations settlement land is not public camping.
notes: The pin is outside the city so it is not a downtown lot. It is still not a reserved site. Open GeoYukon and check the parcel.
